criteria.criterion: `go run ./tools/copilot-acceptance/kit report <kind> <repo> <vloop> <exit code>`, kind one of run, second, work, verify, gate-review, plan, prints what `report.py <kind> …` printed at the starting point, byte for byte, except the session table; it exits 0 when it printed the report, and 1 with a one-line message on stderr and nothing on stdout when an argument is missing, the kind is unknown, or no command is given.
criteria.evidence: report.go ports each tail of report.py; main.go run() returns 1 with one-line stderr for the refusals; the T3 gate compares byte for byte against the base's report.py and passed; TestReportRefusals asserts exit 1, empty stdout, one-line stderr

criteria.criterion: The session table of each kind (gate-review's `| round | record | …` one included), from its header row through the blank line after it, is replaced by one Sessions block per qualifying run id (in name order; a run id qualifies when `<repo>/.vloop/state/runs/<id>/` and `<repo>/docs/briefs/<id>.loop-brief.md` both exist), each exactly the P2 block: the heading line with the literal command, a fenced copy of `<vloop> metrics <id> --by session`'s stdout run in `<repo>` (or the one line `vloop metrics exited <code>: <stderr trimmed, newlines as spaces>`), the `Session records: <n>, schema-valid <k> (<schema> <c>, …).` line (`Session records: 0.` with none; records without a schema last as `no schema <c>`), one `- <folder>/sessions/<file>: <schema> INVALID`, `: no schema` or `: unreadable` line per record so marked, and, only when a row has denials, the `Permission denials:` part with one `- <run>/<#> <phase> <tool_name>: <text>` line per denial (P1's text rule, newlines as spaces); each block ends with one empty line. With no qualifying run id the table is replaced by `Sessions: no brief with runs.` and a blank line.
criteria.evidence: sessions.go runIDs/sessionBlocks/sessionBlock implement each part; TestReports, TestReportMetricsFails and TestReportNoBriefWithRuns compare with literal expected lines

criteria.criterion: The record lines and counts come from the kit reading the record files itself (folders in name order, records in sequence order) and running `<vloop> schema validate <the record's own schema> <file>` in `<repo>`, so they do not depend on vloop metrics succeeding; a session file that is not JSON counts in n only and is listed as unreadable.
criteria.evidence: sessionBlock reads files via readJSON, validates with e.validate(sch, rel) in repo dir; TestReportMetricsFails shows the counts with metrics failing; TestReportUnreadableRecord

criteria.criterion: Wherever the Python renders a value, the Go program renders it the same way: json.dumps with the input's key order (sorted where the Python passes sort_keys), `", "` and `": "` separators, non-ASCII as lowercase `\uXXXX` (surrogate pairs outside the BMP), no HTML escaping, control characters as the Python escapes them, floats as Python's repr; str()/f-string values as Python writes them (a list's repr, None, True, False, `4.0`, `1e+16`). Where the Python joins two unsorted glob lists (second's run.log and iterations.jsonl), each list is taken in sorted path order, the `*/*/` list first.
criteria.evidence: pyval.go has an ordered pyDict, dumps, pyStr and floatRepr; TestPyRendering pins them; secondTail uses glob then globShallow, each sorted; gate byte-compares fixtures

criteria.criterion: Committed Go tests in the kit compare each report kind on its T2 fixture with its golden, building the expected output from the golden by replacing its first table with the Sessions block(s) the test composes: the fenced stdout of `vloop metrics <run id> --by session` from a vloop built from this tree, run on the same fixture copied into a temporary git repository (`git -C`), and the record and denial lines written literally. The test fails when its own vloop metrics call exits non-zero or prints fewer rows than it pins (at least 2), except on the metrics-exits-1 and no-run-folder fixtures, which have tests of their own; `report` with no kind has a test (exit 1, stderr message). Tests build their fixtures in temporary directories and address them with `git -C`; no test runs a real agent CLI, touches `~/.claude` or `~/.copilot`, or needs the network. No go test needs python3; tests that need a shell skip on Windows.
criteria.evidence: report_test.go: TestReports covers six kinds with replaceTable over goldens, block.text fatals on non-zero or fewer than 2 rows; separate r3 and r4 tests; TestReportRefusals includes the no-kind case; fixtures in t.TempDir with git -C; no python and no shell used (checks log shows the kit package ok)

criteria.criterion: The diff changes nothing under tools/copilot-acceptance/kit/testdata/ — the goldens and fixtures are T2's, the Python's output; a golden that seems wrong is reported in the notes, not edited or regenerated from the Go program.
criteria.evidence: git status shows no change under kit/testdata

criteria.criterion: The kit builds with GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows, adds no module dependency, and writes nothing to the repository tree when run.
criteria.evidence: go.mod/go.sum are unchanged and imports are stdlib only; the kit only reads the repository; the go check passed. Cross builds are not shown in the go.log tail, and the code uses no platform-specific API
